title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's sequel to the 'Longue Marche' (1981), on the 'equation of loops' in genus 0 with 3 points. The ambient group is T^+_{0,3}, the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3. It has generators σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). Π_{0,3} is the profinite free group on two generators, the kernel of the map to S_3. ε_0 = σ_∞ρ is the parabolic element, and l_0 = ε_0^2 ∈ Π_{0,3} is the loop around 0. A 'structure à lacets' is the conjugacy class of ε_0, i.e. the inertia data.

The group N^{!~}_{0,3} consists of automorphisms u of T^+_{0,3} that:
- stabilise Π_{0,3},
- induce the identity on S_3,
- send ε_0 to a conjugate of a power ε_0^μ, with μ ∈ Ẑ^*.

Such a u is written u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞, u(ρ) = gρ, with h, g ∈ Π_{0,3}. The order relations (24)/(25) are hσ_∞(h) = 1 and gρ(g)ρ^2(g) = 1, where x(y) denotes conjugation.

This page converts the inertia condition u(ε_0) = f^{-1}ε_0^μ f into a relation among h, g, f:
1. u(ε_0) = hσ_∞ gρ = h σ_∞(g) ε_0.
2. Hence f h σ_∞(g) ε_0 f^{-1} = ε_0^μ.
3. Use ε_0 f^{-1} = ε_0(f^{-1}) ε_0 = σ_∞(ρ(f)^{-1}) ε_0. This gives f h σ_∞(g ρ(f)^{-1}) = ε_0^{μ-1}.
4. Since μ is a unit of Ẑ, its 2-adic component is odd. So ν = (μ-1)/2 ∈ Ẑ exists, and ε_0^{μ-1} = l_0^ν.
5. Conjugating by σ_∞, with σ_∞(l_0) = l_1, gives the boxed loop relation (29): σ_∞(h) g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f).

The margin notes that:
- ν is uniquely determined by (g, h);
- μ = 2ν+1 is the multiplier, i.e. the cyclotomic character in the Galois case.
The final NB adds the 'condition liminaire': h, g, f must actually give an automorphism (the images must generate), not merely an endomorphism. Grothendieck says this will be tacitly assumed from now on.

The next page writes g = [α_0, ρ] and h = [β_0, σ_∞]. This turns (29) into (34), a GT-type relation. There ν plays the role of Drinfeld's m = (λ-1)/2, and f plays the role of the 'f' of a GT element.

Purpose: an explicit, computational description of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group as inertia-preserving automorphisms of the profinite modular group.
errors: No mathematical error found. Each step checks: u(ε_0) = hσ_∞(g)ε_0; ε_0(x) = σ_∞(ρ(x)); the existence of (μ-1)/2 in Ẑ; σ_∞^2 = 1 acting trivially by conjugation.

Minor point on the previous page: f is determined only modulo left multiplication by l_0^n, since the centraliser of ε_0^μ meets Π_{0,3} in the closed subgroup generated by l_0. The machine transcription 'h^n f' there should read 'l_0^n f', as on the next page.

ideas.what: Describe the GT-type group as automorphisms of the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3 that preserve Π_{0,3}, act trivially on S_3 and preserve the inertia class of ε_0 up to a power μ ∈ Ẑ^*
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group via automorphisms of \hat{PSL_2(Z)} / \hat{B_3} (Teichmüller tower in genus 0, level 0,3)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s); Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura–Schneps for the PSL2/B3 formulations
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches the Teichmüller tower and the action on \hat{π}_{0,3}; La Longue Marche (1981) works with \hat{T}_{0,3}. The explicit formulas are probably only in these notes.

ideas.what: Loop (inertia) relation σ_∞(h)g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f), with ν = (μ-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Hexagon/3-cycle relation of GT, f(x,y)x^m f(z,x)z^m f(y,z)y^m = 1 with m = (λ-1)/2, in a 'raw' form

ideas.what: Requiring surjectivity ('condition liminaire') separately from the presentation relations
ideas.modern_name: Invertibility condition in the definition of \hat{GT} (f invertible / generates)

missed.claim: These notes derive the GT parameter relation ν = (μ-1)/2, i.e. the 'm = (λ-1)/2' of Drinfeld's GT, together with a hexagon-type relation, directly from inertia preservation in the profinite modular group. This is an independent and probably earlier derivation than Drinfeld's 1990 definition. It is of historical rather than mathematical interest; the content is now standard.
missed.quote: ν =df (μ-1)/2 ∈ Ẑ ... σ_∞(h) g = σ_∞(f)^{-1} l_1^ν ρ(f) (relation des lacets en h, g, f)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Priority and history of the GT group; the PSL2-based normalisation (σ_∞, ρ, ε_0) may be a useful alternative bookkeeping for GT computations.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, explicit derivation of the GT 3-cycle/inertia relation and of the parameter (μ-1)/2 within the profinite modular group. The mathematics is now standard (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps). What is notable is mainly historical: Grothendieck's own computational path to GT in unpublished notes.
transcription_corrections: Top margin: reads 'relations des lacets dans \hat{Π}_{0,3} (forme brute)' (continuing the margin note of the previous page), not '\hat{π}_{0,3}' with braces.
Lower-left margin probably reads: 'NB ν ∈ Ẑ est uniquement déterminé par g, h, et μ = 2ν+1 ∈ Ẑ^* est le multiplicateur cyclotomique...'.

Final NB: probably 'Il faut de plus exiger, pour que h, g, f définissent un automorphisme, que (23) soit une ... [présentation/génération] de \hat{T}^+_{0,3} — par la suite, nous sous-entendrons toujours tacitement cette "condition liminaire"'. 'contour' and 'sous-présentation' are dubious readings.
In the underbrace, 'h σ_∞(g)' — the transcription's '(gρ)' rendering of the first factor is correct.
